description: pyshop fixture: a Python e-commerce order service (HTTP handlers, order state machine, retrying payment client, repository layer, pricing rules, fulfilment worker). Tasks are phrased the way a developer would describe the problem, deliberately avoiding the identifier names so the corpus measures semantic retrieval rather than substring matching.

cases.task: stop sending traffic to the card processor once it has failed several times in a row, and let a single request through later to see if it recovered
spread out repeated attempts so a whole fleet of workers does not hit the provider again at the exact same moment after an outage
make sure a checkout that gets submitted twice from a flaky mobile client cannot bill the shopper twice
work out which upstream responses are worth another attempt and which ones mean the card was refused and we should give up straight away
stop an order that was already refunded from sliding back into the shipping flow
the queue delivers the same message twice and the second delivery should be a harmless no-op instead of an error
drop the carriage charge once the basket is large enough, and charge a flat rate otherwise
take a little off the basket automatically for shoppers who come back often or sit in a premium band
reject a coupon the shop has never heard of before we bother pricing the whole basket
let several background processes pull work off the same queue table without blocking each other on the same rows
keep the username and password out of the connection string we print at startup
refuse to boot with a clear message when a mandatory environment variable has not been set
adding two amounts in different currencies should blow up loudly instead of quietly coercing one of them
let the long-running loop finish the batch it is holding before the container is torn down
when the polling loop keeps blowing up cycle after cycle, make it wait a while instead of spinning hot
hand a paid basket to the courier and record the parcel number against it
tell the API client the bank said no, with a specific status code rather than a generic server error
put an upper bound on how many distinct products one basket may contain and complain about a bad quantity before anything is saved
